arxiv-2103-08507.title: HepLib : A C++ Library for High Energy Physics Journal: Computer Physics Communications
arxiv-2103-08507.creator: Feng Feng, Yi-Fan Xie, Qiu-Chen Zhou, Shan-Rong Tang
arxiv-2103-08507.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Feng Feng, Yi-Fan Xie, Qiu-Chen Zhou, Shan-Rong Tang. HepLib is a C++ Lib rary for computations in H igh E nergy P hysics, it works on top of GiNaC , a well-established C++ library used to perform symbolic computations. HepLib combines serval well-known packages to get high efficiency, including qgraf to generate Feynman aptitudes, FORM to perform Dirac/Color matrix related computations, and FIRE or KIRA for integration-by-parts (IBP) reduction.

arxiv-2205-06953.title: Topological indices of general relativity and Yang–Mills theory in four-dimensional space-time
arxiv-2205-06953.creator: Yoshimasa Kurihara
arxiv-2205-06953.description: Abstract This report investigates general relativity and the Yang–Mills theory in four-dimensional space-time using a common mathematical framework, the Chern–Weil theory for principal bundles. The whole theory is described owing to the fibre bundle with the G ​ L ​ ( 4 ) GL(4) symmetry by twisting several principal bundles with the gauge symmetry.

arxiv-2309-07432.title: SpatialCodec: Neural Spatial Speech Coding
arxiv-2309-07432.creator: Zhongweiyang Xu ⋆ , Yong Xu † , Vinay Kothapally † , Heming Wang ♯ , Muqiao Yang ‡ , Dong Yu †
arxiv-2309-07432.description: Abstract In this work, we address the challenge of encoding speech captured by a microphone array using deep learning techniques with the aim of preserving and accurately reconstructing crucial spatial cues embedded in multi-channel recordings. We propose a neural spatial audio coding framework that achieves a high compression ratio, leveraging single-channel neural sub-band codec and SpatialCodec.

arxiv-2310-05973.title: Observation of strong attenuation within the photonic band gap of multiconnected networks
arxiv-2310-05973.creator: Pengbo Zhu, Runkai Chen, Xiangbo Yang, Yanglong Fan, Huada Lian, Zhen-Yu Wang
arxiv-2310-05973.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Pengbo Zhu, Runkai Chen, Xiangbo Yang, Yanglong Fan, Huada Lian, Zhen-Yu Wang. We theoretically and experimentally study a photonic band gap (PBG) material made of coaxial cables. The coaxial cables are waveguides for the electromagnetic waves and provide paths for direct wave interference within the material. Using multiconnected coaxial cables to form a unit cell, we realize PBGs via (i) direct interference between the waveguides within each cell and (ii) scattering among different cells.

arxiv-2312-08033.title: Beyond Top-Class Agreement: Using Divergences to Forecast Performance under Distribution Shift
arxiv-2312-08033.creator: Mona Schirmer, Dan Zhang, Eric Nalisnick
arxiv-2312-08033.description: Abstract Knowing if a model will generalize to data ‘in the wild’ is crucial for safe deployment. To this end, we study model disagreement notions that consider the full predictive distribution - specifically disagreement based on Hellinger distance, Jensen-Shannon and Kullback–Leibler divergence.

arxiv-2412-17719.title: Revisiting the Inert Scalar Dark Matter with Vector-like Quarks
arxiv-2412-17719.creator: Prasanta Kumar Das, Shyamashish Dey, Saumyen Kundu, Santosh Kumar Rai
arxiv-2412-17719.description: Abstract The inert doublet model (IDM), a minimal extension of the Standard Model (SM), provides a scalar dark matter (DM) candidate that belongs to the additional Higgs doublet. The model faces challenges in achieving the correct relic abundance for compressed spectra and DM masses in the high-mass range.

arxiv-2501-02648.title: Representation Learning of Lab Values via Masked AutoEncoders
arxiv-2501-02648.creator: David Restrepo, Chenwei Wu, Yueran Jia, Jaden K. Sun, Jack Gallifant, Catherine G. Bielick, Yugang Jia, Leo A. Celi
arxiv-2501-02648.description: Abstract Accurate imputation of missing laboratory values in electronic health records (EHRs) is critical to enable robust clinical predictions and reduce biases in AI systems in healthcare. Existing methods, such as XGBoost, softimpute, GAIN, Expectation Maximization (EM), and MICE, struggle to model the complex temporal and contextual dependencies in EHR data, particularly in underrepresented groups.

arxiv-2504-03549.title: Splash in an inhomogeneous gas in one dimension: Exact analysis and molecular dynamics simulations
arxiv-2504-03549.creator: Amit Kumar, R. Rajesh
arxiv-2504-03549.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Amit Kumar, R. Rajesh. We investigate the splash phenomenon resulting from the energy input at the interface between a vacuum and an inhomogeneous gas with density profile ρ ⁡ ( r ) = ρ 0 ​ r − β \rho(r)=\rho_{0}r^{-\beta} . The energy input causes the formation of ballistic spatters that propagate into the vacuum, leading to a decay of the total energy in the inhomogeneous medium following a power law, E ⁡ ( t ) ∼ t − δ s E(t)\sim t^{-\delta_{s}} .

arxiv-2505-03755.title: Enabling Multireference Calculations on Multi-Metallic Systems with Graphic Processing Units
arxiv-2505-03755.creator: Valay Agarawal, Rishu Khurana, Cong Liu, Matthew R. Hermes, Christopher Knight, Laura Gagliardi
arxiv-2505-03755.description: Abstract Modeling multimetallic systems efficiently enables faster prediction of desirable chemical properties and design of new materials. This work describes an initial implementation for performing multireference wave function method localized active space self-consistent field (LASSCF) calculations through the use of multiple graphics processing units (GPUs) to accelerate time-to-solution.

arxiv-2510-12908.title: Local Differential Privacy for Federated Learning with Fixed Memory Usage and Per-Client Privacy
arxiv-2510-12908.creator: Rouzbeh Behnia University of South Florida behnia@usf.edu and Jeremiah Birrell Texas State University jbirrell@txstate.edu and Arman Riasi Virginia Tech armanriasi@vt.edu and Reza Ebrahimi University of South Florida ebrahimim@usf.edu and Kaushik Dutta University of South Florida duttak@usf.edu and
arxiv-2510-12908.description: Abstract Abstract Federated learning (FL) enables organizations to collaboratively train models without sharing their datasets. Despite this advantage, recent studies show that both client updates and the global model can leak private information, limiting adoption in sensitive domains such as healthcare. Local differential privacy (LDP) offers strong protection by letting each participant privatize updates before transmission.

arxiv-2601-20812.title: Effective Sample Size for Functional Spatial Data
arxiv-2601-20812.creator: Alfredo Alegría 1 , John Gómez 2 , Jorge Mateu 3 , and Ronny Vallejos 2
arxiv-2601-20812.description: Abstract The effective sample size quantifies the amount of independent information contained in a dataset, accounting for redundancy due to correlation between observations. While widely used in geostatistics for scalar data, its extension to functional spatial data has remained largely unexplored.

pmc-10601711.title: Molecular landscape and clinical significance of exon 11 mutations in KIT gene among patients with gastrointestinal stromal tumor: a retrospective exploratory study
pmc-10601711.creator: Ruihua Zhao, Tianqi An, Min Liu, Yanan Zhou, Rui Li, Guozhong Jiang, Jing Li, Xinguang Cao, Hong Zong

pmc-11559703.title: Validation of the Arabic version of the Obstructive Sleep Apnea-18 quality of life questionnaire for evaluating children with sleep apnea–hypopnea syndrome
pmc-11559703.creator: Montaha Al-Iede, Mohammad Ali Alshrouf, Abdallah Al-Ani, Alaa Alkurdi, Areej H. Jaber, Omar Husain, Batool Abusabra, Nihad A. Almasri
pmc-11559703.description: BACKGROUND:Pediatric obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) poses a significant health concern, affecting the well-being and quality of life of affected children. This study focuses on the translation, adaptation, and validation of the OSA-18 questionnaire for Arabic-speaking pediatric patients, aiming to contribute to the understanding of OSA and its implications on the quality of life in this population.

pmc-11670233.title: What is the Gold Standard for Advanced Hallux Rigidus? Minimum 10 Year Follow-Up Comparison of Interposition Arthroplasty and Arthrodesis Shows Similar Outcomes
pmc-11670233.creator: Jeffrey E. Johnson, Andrea R. Phinney, Mary Hastings, Hyo Jung Jeong, Ling Chen, Andrew P. Thome, Jeremy J. McCormick, Jonathon D. Backus
pmc-11670233.description: Category:Midfoot/Forefoot; OtherIntroduction/ Purpose:Hallux rigidus is characterized by arthritic changes of the first metatarsophalangeal joint (MTPJ) with joint space narrowing, osteophyte formation, and painful MTPJ motion. Although MTPJ arthrodesis is considered the “gold standard,” a Modified Oblique Keller Capsular Interposition Arthroplasty (MOKCIA) is an alternative treatment for hallux rigidus in patients who desire to retain MTPJ motion.

pmc-12875972.title: Influencing factors of initiation and maintenance of multidomain interventions in patients with mild cognitive impairment: a qualitative study
pmc-12875972.creator: Yuxin Han, Qing Wang, Jianing Shao, Jiachen Zhang, Xiaomin Zhang, Shaoting Sheng
pmc-12875972.description: BackgroundMild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a critical period for the prevention of dementia, and multidomain interventions can effectively delay and improve patients’ cognitive decline. However, it remains a great challenge concerning the initiation and maintenance of interventions for MCI patients currently.ObjectiveTo explore influencing factors of the initiation and maintenance of multidomain interventions in patients with MCI.

pmc-13013681.title: Chaotic fluctuations mark the sign of mental activity in task-based heart rate variability
pmc-13013681.creator: Tomoyuki Mao, Hidetoshi Okutomi, Ken Umeno
pmc-13013681.description: Heart rate variability (HRV), regulated by the autonomic nervous system, is typically assessed using standard time-domain and frequency-domain methods to evaluate autonomic function. However, conventional linear analyses capture only a limited aspect of HRV, as the human body, including the cardiovascular system, is intrinsically nonlinear.

pmc-13099809.title: Mindfulness as a mediator between intolerance of uncertainty and test anxiety among adolescents: a structural equation model
pmc-13099809.creator: Ahmet Sapanci, Hamdi Korkman, Mark D. Griffiths
pmc-13099809.description: Test anxiety is a prevalent problem among adolescents and is closely associated with cognitive and emotional responses to uncertainty. Although intolerance of uncertainty and mindfulness have each been linked to anxiety, their joint role within a unified explanatory model remains insufficiently explored.

pmc-13590607.title: Conception-calibrated male pediatric tumor mitotic clocks
pmc-13590607.creator: Jeremiah V. John, Darryl Shibata
pmc-13590607.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Molecular clocks can reconstruct tumorigenesis, but their calibration is limited by uncertainty in cancer ages. Pediatric cancers simplify this problem because age ranges are narrowly bounded by conception and a minimum of ~30 divisions. We developed mitotic clocks from rapidly fluctuating CpG (fCpG) DNA methylation on the X chromosome in male cancers, applying a two-state Markov model to estimate mitotic age and epimutation rates.

pmc-13602511.title: Optimizing COVID-19 vaccination for older adults: superior efficacy of heterologous regimens in reducing infection and mortality rates among patients aged 80 years and older during the Omicron BA.5/BF.7 outbreak
pmc-13602511.creator: Songlin Qiu, Yijun Chen, Awei Sheng, Bo Shen, Sailing He, Yufen Zheng
pmc-13602511.description: BackgroundFollowing the adjustment of COVID-19 control policies in mainland China, particularly during the Omicron BA.5 and BF.7 waves, evaluating vaccine effectiveness in individuals aged ≥ 80 years is of critical importance.Patients and methodsThis retrospective study included 2,325 hospitalized patients aged 80 years and older from four hospitals between December 9, 2022, and January 27, 2023.

pmc-13663477.title: JAK3-Mediated Structural Remodeling of β-Catenin Suppresses Epithelial–Mesenchymal Transition: Insights from In Silico Modeling
pmc-13663477.creator: Jugal Kishore Das, Jayshree Mishra, Narendra Kumar
pmc-13663477.description: Simple SummaryJanus kinase 3 (JAK3) is a non-receptor tyrosine kinase that interacts with and phosphorylates several proteins, including β-catenin, a key component of adherens junctions (AJs). We previously demonstrated that JAK3-mediated phosphorylation of β-catenin regulates its localization to the basolateral membrane and is essential for maintaining epithelial barrier integrity.
